ox.service.checkAccess.description: Read the applicable access evidence advertised by inspect without prompting. Website checks return sessions; API checks return configuration, not server acceptance; MCP checks return connectivity, not tool authorization; native checks return permission. Errors are not absence. Reuse a selected website descriptor; protected invocations revalidate it.

pageUrl.description: Website-only discovery target within the service domain.

ox.service.requestAccess.description: Use the applicable contract from inspect.access to request website login, API credential setup, MCP authorization, or device permission. Optional input matches the website's login schema; pageUrl is website-only. Website completion acknowledges interaction, not authentication: checkAccess afterward. Never automatically reopen cancellation or replay writes.

pageUrl.description: Website-only initial login target within the service domain.

ox.service.showPage.description: Show the existing live page used by a web service action for user review or takeover: `await ox.service.showPage({ purpose, name, input?, session?, pageUrl? })`. When the user asks to see a service action's page, call this function rather than substituting a Markdown URL link. A linked page can share website session storage without sharing the action's live document. Pass the same qualified action name, input, and session or pageUrl used by ox.service.invoke to select its execution page. This does not invoke the action, navigate, reload, submit, or create a replacement page. Waits until the user dismisses the page and preserves it afterward. The user can interact with the live website; dismissal does not verify its contents or prove submission. Inspect fresh service state before dependent work. Throws if no idle live page exists or presentation is unavailable. Use this for showing prepared applications or drafts, not ox.web.browser.showPage, which presents only the authoring Browser. Use ox.service.requestAccess for account setup; showPage does not start login. Use this same flow for human verification and payment: prepare the visible challenge or checkout through ordinary service actions, then show its live page. The user completes verification or commits payment and marks completion; no completion detection runs. Never submit payment from preparation actions or automatically repeat writes after dismissal.

name.description: The same qualified web action name used for the page's invocation.

input.description: The same action input, used only to select its execution page.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.attach.description: Attach an Ox Server service by domain after inspecting its `services/<kind>/<id>/service.json`: `await ox.service.attach({ purpose, domain })`. The first call saves and attaches the service to this conversation; a later call reloads that conversation's attachment from the current service source so a coherent set of Local edits can be tested. Source writes do not reload running attachments. The first attach is allowed by default and respects configured Action policies. If approval is required and the user declines, this throws, so surface that and don't retry blindly. Returns the service snapshot with `reloaded` indicating whether an existing attachment was replaced; a `requireAuth` action revalidates before use. `purpose` is a short (<10 words) human-readable description shown to the user as the step label.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.copy.description: Copy the selected Bundled, Development, or Remote service into the editable Local repository and select that candidate: `await ox.service.copy({ purpose, domain })`. Edit its expanded source under `services/` with `ox.fs`. If a Local copy already exists, inspect ox.repository.conflicts and select that Local candidate with ox.repository.resolve; never overwrite it to resolve a conflict. iOS services are not authorable.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.create.description: Create a Local API service with kind api and a stable domain identifier, a Local web service with `{ purpose, kind: "web", domain }`, or save a remote MCP connection with `{ purpose, kind: "mcp", endpoint, transport?, faviconUrl? }`. faviconUrl is an optional public HTTPS PNG, JPEG, or ICO URL; anonymous loading permits up to five public HTTPS redirects. MCP saves without connecting or requesting login; explicitly inspect tools and use requestAccess when needed after saving it to the Local repository at `services/mcp/<domain>/service.json`; it returns the assigned domain, derived from the endpoint host, for inspect/attach/invoke/delete. An existing endpoint is reused; use update to change its settings or refresh tools. MCP connections save immediately. Never put credentials in the endpoint; use requestAccess. This connects to a server, not hosts one.

endpoint.description: Public HTTPS MCP endpoint without credentials. Required for MCP; omit domain.

faviconUrl.description: Optional public HTTPS PNG, JPEG, or ICO URL for this MCP connection.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.delete.description: Delete a Local web service or remove an MCP connection: `await ox.service.delete({ purpose, domain })`. The user approves deletion. Inspect the target source before deleting it and preserve unrelated work. For web services, source deletion is immediate and another repository candidate may become active. There is no built-in version history to restore deleted source. MCP removal is immediate, deletes a Local definition, detaches it from this conversation, clears local authorization and tool approvals, and does not revoke access at the server or delete a non-Local repository definition.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.detach.description: Detach a service (by domain) from this conversation: `await ox.service.detach({ purpose, domain })`. Removes it from the conversation's attachment bar so its actions stop being available; the service stays saved. Use when the user is done with it or you attached the wrong one. Returns the service snapshot (`attached: false`). `purpose` is a short (<10 words) human-readable description shown to the user as the step label.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.find.description: Search enabled service repositories when no attached service covers the task: `await ox.service.find({ purpose, query })`. Returns up to ten ranked matches (domain, kind, manifestPath, repository, repositoryProvenance, name, description, matchedAction, login, saved, attached). Read a strong candidate's manifest when needed, then attach it through normal Action policies without a separate consent prompt. Empty results establish only that enabled repositories have no match; discovery failure does not establish absence. For an unconfigured MCP server or API, use supplied endpoints or public research of official documentation through evolve. When website coverage is missing, build the needed action through Evolve, then invoke it; Browser is only for authoring and repair.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

query.description: What the user wants to do, in a few words (e.g. "stream music", "order food").

outputSchema.description: Array of service snapshots, best match first.

ox.service.inspect.description: Inspect one attached service: `await ox.service.inspect({ purpose, domain, actions? })`. Omit `actions` for a compact business-action index; website discovery/login implementations are represented by access helpers rather than duplicate action entries. Pass up to ten exposed action IDs to receive their complete, self-contained input and output schemas. Both forms include access.kind and only the applicable checkAccess/requestAccess helper contracts under access. capabilitiesAvailable:false means tool discovery failed, not that the service has no actions; inspect capabilityError before requesting setup or retrying. Human verification and payment use ordinary preparation actions followed by ox.service.showPage; there are no specialized helper contracts.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

outputSchema.description: The attached service snapshot, an action-keyed map of summaries or complete schemas, and applicable typed access helper contracts.

ox.service.invoke.description: Invoke a service action: `await ox.service.invoke({ purpose, name, input?, session?, pageUrl? })`. Copy the qualified name and exact input shape from ox.service.inspect; names use web:<domain>:<action>, api:<service>:<action>, ios:<app>:<action>, or mcp:<server>:<action>. Inspect full input/output contracts before invocation. Runtime Action approval is authoritative; never invent approval fields or repeat a denied call. For session-aware websites, use inspect.access.checkAccess to discover sessions once and copy a returned descriptor into top-level session; handlers receive it as second-argument context.session. Optional pageUrl selects a public HTTPS initial target within the service domain for discovery, login or public work; do not combine it with session. Use inspect.access.requestAccess for login, then checkAccess again; completion acknowledges interaction, not authentication. A page is not a session. Never fabricate descriptors or silently switch accounts. Session-aware requireAuth actions require a selected descriptor; the Host checks fresh listSessions evidence before dispatch. Reuse the selected descriptor rather than adding an access check before every action; rediscover after login, expiry or an account switch. Snapshot login fields are not proof of current website authentication or API acceptance. Account-sensitive handlers must still verify their actual account and target. Failed or incomplete calls may have effects; inspect resulting state before retrying writes. Treat empty, partial, or implausible results as possible defects; cross-check them with Browser tools or another query before reporting absence. When a needed web or API action is missing or confirmed defective, read Evolve, build or repair the action, then invoke it to complete the request. Use Browser only for service authoring and repair, never as a fulfillment fallback. Report concrete authoring blockers. MCP and iOS services cannot be changed; report the limit.

input.description: Input matching the action's inputSchema returned by `ox.service.inspect`.

pageUrl.description: Initial target URL for session discovery, login, or public actions; cannot be combined with session.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

outputSchema.description: The action's output, which varies by the schema returned by `ox.service.inspect`.

ox.service.list.description: List all available services from enabled repositories, sorted by domain: `await ox.service.list({ purpose, kind? })`. Filter by `kind: "web"` for website services, `kind: "api"` for HTTP API services, `kind: "ios"` for device services, or `kind: "mcp"` for remote MCP servers. Every result includes its kind and current conversation attachment state. Returns every service without a result limit; omits action contracts. Disabled repositories are excluded.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

outputSchema.description: Array of available service snapshots with domain, name, description when present, kind, login, saved, attached, and repository or MCP connection metadata when applicable.

ox.service.listAttached.description: List the services currently attached to this conversation: `await ox.service.listAttached({ purpose, kind? })`. Filter by `kind: "web"` for website services, `kind: "api"` for HTTP API services, `kind: "ios"` for device services, or `kind: "mcp"` for remote MCP servers. Every result includes its kind.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.update.description:
Update an existing service by domain: `await ox.service.update({ purpose, domain, ...fields })`. Supported fields depend on the existing service kind; unsupported fields are rejected, and omitted fields are preserved. This never creates a missing service or changes its kind. All service kinds and repository sources support name as a local display-name override, applied immediately and preserved across restarts and source refreshes. Renaming leaves service identity, action names, source manifests, connections, and authorization unchanged.

Local web services support description, baseUrl, faviconUrl, actions, and $defs. Local API services support those fields plus auth. Read the current manifest before updating. Arrays and objects replace the whole field, not merge; null removes optional description, faviconUrl, or $defs. Identity is fixed. Source updates validate the resulting manifest and write atomically but do not validate handlers or reload attachments. Edit actions.js with ox.fs; finish the draft, call ox.service.validate, then ox.service.attach to load/reload. Changing API baseUrl or auth requires setup again. Credentials never belong in source. Bundled, Development, and Remote sources are read-only; copy eligible web/API services to Local before updating. Native services support only name.

Local MCP connections additionally support endpoint, transport, and faviconUrl. MCP also accepts a connection name or unique endpoint host as domain. With no fields, reconnects and refreshes tools; a name-only update does not reconnect. Set transport to auto for detection. Set faviconUrl to a public HTTPS PNG, JPEG, or ICO URL, or null to restore server-advertised icons. Explicit icons load anonymously with up to five public HTTPS redirects; server-advertised icons remain same-site without redirects. Connection changes validate before replacing and save immediately; failure preserves the old connection. Changing endpoint keeps the domain but clears old local authorization and tool approvals. Tool contracts and implementation belong to the server and cannot be edited here. Other repositories' MCP connection settings are read-only; copy them to Local before changing connection settings.

$defs.description: Replace Local web/API shared JSON Schema definitions; null removes them.

actions.description: Replace the complete Local web/API action declarations. Handlers remain in actions.js; edit them with ox.fs and validate before attaching.

auth.description: Replace Local API authentication configuration, never credentials. Supported objects: {type: 'none'}; {type: 'apiKey', in: 'header'|'query', name: '<header-or-query-name>'}; {type: 'http', scheme: 'basic'|'bearer'}; or {type: 'oauth2', flow: 'authorizationCode', authorizationURL: '<HTTPS URL>', tokenURL: '<HTTPS URL>', clientID: '<registered public client>', redirectURI: '<app callback URI>', scopes: ['<scope>'], pkce: 'S256'}. OAuth endpoints cannot contain credentials, query, or fragment; callback uses a non-HTTP app scheme without query or fragment. Requires setup again.

baseUrl.description: Local web execution URL or API HTTPS base URL. Web URLs must remain on the service domain or its subdomains.

description.description: Local web/API description; null removes it.

domain.description: Existing service domain. Direct MCP also accepts a saved connection name or unique endpoint host.

faviconUrl.description: Public HTTPS PNG, JPEG, or ICO URL. Local web/API and direct MCP support this field; null removes a Local override or restores MCP-advertised icons.

name.description: Local display name for any service kind.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.validate.description: Validate a complete Local web or API service draft: `await ox.service.validate({ purpose, domain })`. Checks the manifest, action installer and matching action IDs, required files, and service size limits together. Reusable skills are independent packages verified through evolve. Returns `{ domain, valid: true }` or throws with the validation error. Does not edit, attach, reload, Save, or invoke service actions. Finish related source edits before calling; individual file writes do not validate service contents.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.
